name: A4950ELJTR-T
title: A4950: full-bridge DMOS PWM driver for a brushed DC motor, 40 V, ±3.5 A
summary: One H-bridge of N-channel DMOS switches for a single brushed DC motor, run from 8 V to 40 V and good for peaks of ±3.5 A. Two logic inputs, IN1 and IN2, pick forward, reverse, brake or coast, and an external PWM on them sets speed. An optional sense resistor on LSS together with the VREF voltage sets a chopping current limit with a fixed 25 µs off-time; the bridge rectifies synchronously, and it guards against shorted outputs, undervoltage, overtemperature and shoot-through. A4950ELJTR-T is the -40 °C to 85 °C grade in an 8-pin SOIC with an exposed pad.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The A4950 drives one brushed DC motor connected across OUT1 and OUT2 from the VBB supply. IN1 and IN2 come from the controller and set direction and PWM; VREF sets the chopping current limit through RS, a 0.25 Ω sense resistor from LSS to ground (2 A with VREF at 5 V). VBB is decoupled by a 0.22 µF ceramic, C1, next to the pin and a 100 µF electrolytic, C2. GND and the exposed pad share the ground.

operation.text: All four switches are low-RDS(on) N-channel DMOS. IN1 and IN2 give two-wire control: one high drives the motor one way, the other high drives it the other way, both high brakes and both low lets it coast. Speed comes from PWM applied to the inputs.

Holding both inputs low for more than 1 ms puts the part into Low Power Standby, which shuts off most of the circuitry including the charge pump and the regulator; supply current drops to 10 µA max. On leaving standby, wait for the charge pump to come up (30 µs at most) before sending PWM.

A diagonal source/sink pair conducts and the current builds through the motor and RS. Once ten times the LSS voltage reaches VREF, the comparator clears the PWM latch and the bridge enters mixed decay for the fixed off-time toff (25 µs typ).

Each off-time starts with fast decay for half of toff and finishes with slow decay. On every changeover the drivers are all held off for the crossover delay tCOD to stop shoot-through; synchronous rectification is inactive during that interval.

While current recirculates in the off-time, the matching DMOS switches are turned on so the current bypasses the body diodes, cutting dissipation. Rectification stops when the current reaches zero, so it never reverses in the load.
A current monitor catches a shorted motor or an output shorted to ground or to the supply, latches the fault and disables the outputs. Only leaving Low Power Standby or cycling VBB clears the latch.

Near 160 °C die temperature the bridge outputs switch off and stay off until the die cools by the 15 °C hysteresis. Undervoltage lockout on VBB keeps the outputs off until the supply is above the threshold (7.5 V typ rising).

Driving both inputs high after a chop command puts the bridge in slow decay, shorting the motor's back-EMF through the switches, which conduct both ways. In heavy braking cases, such as a fast motor or a high-inertia load, the current must stay within the maximum ratings.

Current control needs a low-value resistor from LSS to ground. Give it its own short return to the star ground so trace IR drop does not shift the sensed current; with very small resistors that drop is significant. The LSS limit is ±500 mV at maximum load, which may be exceeded briefly in an overcurrent event.

Place a star ground as near the device as possible; the copper under the exposed pad serves well, with the pad grounded. Use a thick ground plane, solder the part straight to the board and the pad to exposed copper, and use thermal vias to carry heat to other layers. Decouple VBB with an electrolytic of about 100 µF plus a smaller ceramic as close to the pin as practical.
